repository_evidence.bounded_search_scope: Campaign160 inventory and Campaign163-204 source-frontier metadata only
repository_evidence.asset_license_incident_boundary: Campaign166, Campaign178 and Campaign179 freeze discrete incidents, productive assets and licenses or concessions. Spectrum, towers, fiber, switches, data centers, capex, a license or one outage does not preserve subscriber, service-order, number, SIM or eSIM, session, allowance, charge, bill, delinquency, suspension and reconnection identities across the complete applicable population.
repository_evidence.operating_kpi_boundary: Campaign168 freezes recurring subscriber, active-user, traffic, coverage, capacity and utilization KPIs. Aggregate subscribers, net additions, ARPU, data traffic, homes passed, ports, minutes, drops or churn do not preserve opening stocks and all provisioning, activation, porting, service, session, charging and closure transitions.
repository_evidence.pricing_customer_quality_and_support_bou: Campaign169 freezes plan and tariff terms, Campaign170 freezes retention, churn and customer-experience outcomes, and Campaign199 freezes support-case stock flow and SLA clocks. A tariff, NPS, complaint, churn rate or support ticket cannot substitute for the underlying telecommunications subscriber, service-delivery, session, charging, billing and reconnection lifecycle.
repository_evidence.payment_loyalty_software_and_accounting_: Campaign195 freezes authorization, clearing, refund and settlement rails; Campaign197 freezes loyalty-unit obligations; Campaign198 freezes software release and installed-version states. Receipts, receivables, contract balances, rewards, app releases, device software or revenue do not establish a complete subscriber-service, network-session, charge, bill, dunning, suspension and reconnection history.
repository_evidence.utility_boundary: Campaign204 demonstrates that superficially similar connection, usage, outage, billing, disconnection and reconnection operators do not create a cross-sector factor. Telecommunications service has distinct identity, number portability, SIM or eSIM, device, plan, allowance, roaming, interconnect, session and rating semantics and requires its own complete source contract.
repository_evidence.privacy_communications_and_critical_infr: No directly identifiable subscriber, personal number, communications content, precise location, contact graph, payment credential, raw call or messaging detail, authentication secret, network-security credential, sensitive topology or operational-control data may be acquired or used. Any admitted source must be lawful, licensed or public and sufficiently deidentified and aggregated to prevent re-identification, surveillance and infrastructure-security harm while preserving the frozen point-in-time issuer-state contract.
repository_evidence.sector_scope_boundary: Applicable listed fixed, mobile, broadband, cable, satellite and converged telecommunications providers, listed parents and material operating subsidiaries must be frozen point in time. Network-equipment vendors, handset makers, software vendors, tower lessors without retail service, resellers without preserved obligations and structurally inapplicable issuers may not be filled with zero or cross-sector ranked.
repository_evidence.point_in_time_boundary: A current subscriber count, coverage map, plan catalog, number inventory, SIM estate, network dashboard, billing balance or churn report cannot be projected backward without application, identity-safe eligibility, order, provisioning, activation, porting, session, rating, allowance, adjustment, dispute, payment, dunning, suspension, reconnection, closure and first-public or first-licensed-availability histories.
